strategy.summary: Reproduce sympy#26821/PR #26822: Matrix.inv and M.exp() over RR[x,y,...] (float-coefficient polynomial matrices) produce huge floats (~1e251) on the buggy commit 66c229001b7d; the fix converts RR to QQ in _inv_DM before inv_den and converts back. Run the two developer tests added to sympy/matrices/tests/test_matrixbase.py; they should fail on the buggy revision and pass on the fixed one. Environment is a source checkout of sympy at the buggy commit (no PyPI release is correct for the bug since it is in-tree code), installed editable, with the test suite run via pytest or sympy's bin/test.

pinned_because: sympy version is unbounded in the evidence (documented constraint null, era_ceiling null); the strategy chooses to test the in-tree source at the buggy commit 66c229001b7d rather than a PyPI release, because the regression is in the repository code under test
mpmath is needed by sympy's numerics and is not pinned by the evidence; the version is left to the installer

strategy.reproducing_test: sympy/matrices/tests/test_matrixbase.py::test_inverse_symbolic_float_issue_26821 and sympy/matrices/tests/test_matrixbase.py::test_matrix_exponential_issue_26821 (the latter is decorated @slow, so it is skipped unless SYMPY_SLOW or sympy's own test runner enables slow tests; run with bin/test or set the slow flag if pytest reports it as skipped)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 66c229001b7d, at least one of the two tests fails: test_inverse_symbolic_float_issue_26821 fails at the assertion max(abs(f) for f in Mi.atoms(Float)) < 1e3 (or earlier at the M*Mi cancel check), and/or test_matrix_exponential_issue_26821 fails at max(abs(f) for f in Me.atoms(Float)) < 1e3 because the atoms reach ~1e251. On the fixed revision (the PR #26822 commit), both tests pass with all Float atoms below 1e3 and the cancel-to-zeros identities holding.
strategy.numerical_probe: Mi = M.inv() for the 7x7 matrix from the test, then print sorted(abs(f) for f in Mi.atoms(Float))[-3:]; buggy value around 1e251, fixed value at most single digits. Used only for diagnosis, not for the pass/fail decision.

input_output_examples.input: M = Matrix([...]) from issue gh-26821 (7x7 with float entries 1.0 and symbols Tau, Tau_syn_in, Tau_syn_ex, C_m, Tau_syn_gap); Mi = M.inv(); Mi.atoms(Float)
input_output_examples.expected_output: Floats of small magnitude only (no values near 1e251); exact rational coefficients over QQ[...]

input_output_examples.input: Me = (t*M).exp() for the gh-26821 matrix with symbol __h and the test's symbols Tau, Tau_syn_in, Tau_syn_ex, C_m, Tau_syn_gap (the matrix in the exp test uses a, b, c, d, e names; the symbol-name difference matters)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Me.atoms(Float) includes values from about -1.14555615673900e+251 to 1.14555615673900e+251

risks: The defect is expressed through floating-point coefficients over RR[...]; it is not architecture-specific in the evidence, so no special platform is required, but the magnitude of the blow-up (~1e251) is environment-dependent; the transition only needs the bound < 1e3 to flip.

Symbol names matter in the original report: Tau_syn_in etc. gave huge floats while aa..ee gave small ones. The exp test uses names 'Tau, Tau_syn_in, ...' via symbols() with a, b, c, d, e variables, so keep the names exactly as in the test diff, not renamed.

The @slow decorator on test_matrix_exponential_issue_26821 means plain pytest may skip it; if it is skipped on both revisions the transition is not observed for that test, so the inverse test is the reliable one to run.

The commit was bisected to 030101630865b039d239f84bc4151cf1c895c6ef (gh-25452); the buggy commit 66c229001b7d is a later state, so confirm the checkout is at the buggy revision and not already containing the fix.

The exact sympy version is unbounded in the evidence; no documented constraint exists, so choosing the in-tree source is a deliberate choice, and PyPI releases may differ in whether the defect appears.
The exp test calls (t*M).exp() which can be slow; the timeout of the harness should accommodate it.
The evidence gives no exact expected float values beyond the 1e3 bound and the small atom set listed in the issue, so pass/fail rests on the bound, not on printed numbers.

oracle.tolerance: max(abs(f) for f in Mi.atoms(Float)) < 1e3 and the cancel-to-zeros check on M*Mi - eye(7) and (Me.diff(t) - M*Me)
oracle.reference_source: test assertions in the PR #26822 diff (test_inverse_symbolic_float_issue_26821 and test_matrix_exponential_issue_26821)
oracle.why: The developer tests assert the bound directly; the transition is decided by whether the float atoms exceed 1e3 on the buggy revision and not on the fixed one.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 66c229001b7d the inverse returns float coefficients around 1e251 so max(abs(f) for f in Mi.atoms(Float)) is far above 1e3, and the assertion fails; likewise the exp test's Me.atoms(Float) contains values near 1e251 so its bound assertion fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision _inv_DM converts RR[...] to QQ[...] via get_exact before inv_den and back afterward, so the float atoms are small and the cancel checks hold; both tests pass.
